payload.title: Bind recovery confirmation to the exact displayed Checkout owner
payload.summary: P1 maintained recovery-authority correspondence. CLI work-recover reads/displays owner A before a default-No prompt. In an explicitly synthetic tiny-fixture terminal callback, A is recovered elsewhere and new active owner B enters before y is returned for displayed A. The CLI calls recover(authorize=True), which rereads B rather than binding A. It returns CHECKOUT_RECOVERED, restores B admitted value=2 to value=0 and removes B claim. Displayed and replaced SHA/PID differ; B PID is the current live probe process. No genuine user approval, actual grant or canonical owner was fabricated.
payload.benefit: Bind the trusted recovery decision to the exact owner identity shown before consent. Pass and reauthenticate that expected identity inside the serialized/fenced recovery admission, refusing changed owner/missing owner/altered source before effects. A changed owner requires a new explicit default-No decision, never automatic yes propagation. Permanent tests must exercise actual CLI before/after-prompt replacement, intact unchanged owner success, denied consent, schema/root mismatch and legitimate process-stopped checks. Preserve API/custody compatibility explicitly and do not turn this into a new authority engine. Run focused/static and full protected validation for eventual source/test correction.
payload.uncertainty: This is separate from a stale finalizer crossing an already acquired new lease: even a single perfectly serialized recovery can reinterpret earlier consent if it loads a different owner after the prompt. Existing coding-grant issue/dispatch already rechecks state after terminal waits; use compatible exact-state semantics here. Terminal I/O was explicitly mocked only in disposable data; this proves the code path, not that a real operator approved B.
